q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an _____.
e: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field. Put magnetic field or gravitational field in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The charging process can be viewed as the apparent transfer of charge from a conductor at lower potential to a conductor at _____ potential.
e: The charging process can be viewed as the apparent transfer of charge from a conductor at lower potential to a conductor at higher potential. Put equal or zero in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: The work done in charging the capacitor is given by the shaded area under the curve in the _____ graph.
e: The work done in charging the capacitor is given by the shaded area under the curve in the Q-V graph. Put I-t or V-I in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential.

q: The electrical energy stored by the capacitor W is equal to _____.
e: The electrical energy stored by the capacitor W is equal to (1)/(2)QV. Put QV or (1)/(4)QV in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: Since $C=Q/V$, the energy, W, of the capacitor can be expressed as W = _____.
e: Since C=Q/V, the energy, W, of the capacitor can be expressed as W = (1)/(2)CV^2. Put CV^2 or (1)/(2)C/V^2 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The energy W of the capacitor can also be expressed in terms of Q and C as W = _____.
e: The energy W of the capacitor can also be expressed in terms of Q and C as W = (1)/(2)Q^2/C. Put (1)/(2)QC or Q^2C in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: Placing a resistor in the charging circuit _____ the charging process.
e: Placing a resistor in the charging circuit slows down the charging process. speeds up is not slows down, and has no effect on is not slows down either. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential.

q: The greater the values of resistance and capacitance, the _____ it takes to charge the capacitor.
e: The greater the values of resistance and capacitance, the longer it takes to charge the capacitor. Put shorter or same time in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: The voltage rises with time during charging according to the equation $V_c =$ _____.
e: The voltage rises with time during charging according to the equation Vc = V0(1 - e^-t/RC). V0 e^-t/RC is not V0(1 - e^-t/RC), and V0(1 + e^-t/RC) is not V0(1 - e^-t/RC) either. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called the _____ of a capacitor charging or discharging process.
e: The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called the time constant of a capacitor charging or discharging process. Put frequency or period in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: The time constant is measured in _____.
e: The time constant is measured in ohms. seconds and farads belong to other processes, not this ohms case. RC is the charging and discharging time scale; after a few RC the exponential has almost settled.

q: The voltage of the capacitor falls off with time during discharging according to the equation $V_c =$ _____.
e: The voltage of the capacitor falls off with time during discharging according to the equation Vc = V0(1 - e^-t/RC). Put V0 e^t/RC or V0 e^-t/RC in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: The energy stored by the capacitor can be analyzed from the _____ graph.
e: The energy stored by the capacitor can be analyzed from the I-t graph. Q-V is not I-t, and V-R is not I-t either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: Before a capacitor is charged, each of its conductors has no charge, and the potential difference between two conductors is _____.
e: Before a capacitor is charged, each of its conductors has no charge, and the potential difference between two conductors is infinite. Put maximum or zero in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.
